clue.text: Flier in dispute after dispute

indicators.note: the first dispute word is placed after the second one in the answer

parts.note: to spar is to argue or dispute
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A bird gets caught up in one quarrel after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs in turn: ROW placed after SPAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small bird, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: Is it a pitfall for the governor?

parts.note: the contraction 's stands for is, as in it's
a pitfall is a trap

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a ruse is laid for the governor.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'it's a trap'. A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia.
explanation.definitionFit: Satraps were provincial rulers in the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: The lute Ada made is flatter

indicators.note: the instrument and the woman's name are fashioned into a new word

explanation.surface: An instrument built by Ada sounds flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like an adjective about pitch; it is the verb. 'made' rearranges LUTEADA.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate someone is to praise them excessively, to fawn on them.

clue.text: Refuse all round, I see — disgusting!

indicators.note: the refusal word goes completely around the other two pieces

parts.note: to repulse is to reject or refuse
taken as written
v is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: Rubbish everywhere, I notice, and it is revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like rubbish; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive causes strong revulsion, much like something revolting.

clue.text: Shelving Light's complaints about the house

parts.note: a light is a window, as in leaded lights
ills are ailments or complaints

explanation.surface: Light's ailments around the house are put aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelving' looks like postponing; it is literal shelves, ledges found about the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Window sills are ledges below windows, a kind of household shelving.

clue.text: Plucky mixed-up type is dished

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for food served in a dish, read here as the thing that is dished

parts.note: game means brave or plucky, as in game for anything
pie is printers' jargon for jumbled printing type

explanation.surface: A brave but confused character is defeated or ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dished' looks like slang for ruined; it is food baked in a dish. PIE is printers' term for a muddle of spilt type.
explanation.definitionFit: A game pie is a savoury pastry of game birds or venison, cooked and served in a dish.

clue.text: What a Lothario in camp !

definitions.meaning: Rowe's play calls its seducer the haughty, gallant, merry Lothario

explanation.definitionFit: Rowe's seducer is famously the 'gay Lothario', meaning merry; the word also means camp or homosexual.

clue.text: Our Sicilian thing

parts.note: translates the Italian name Cosa Nostra, our thing, used for the Sicilian crime syndicate

explanation.surface: Something belonging to us comes from Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosa Nostra, meaning our thing, is the name the Sicilian crime syndicate uses for itself.

clue.text: Mary Robinson played her pant famously

definitions.text: Mary Robinson played her pant famously

parts.words: Mary Robinson played her pant famously
parts.note: the eighteenth-century actress was celebrated as Shakespeare's heroine in The Winter's Tale and kept the role's name as a nickname

explanation.surface: An actress made her name in a role.
explanation.walkthrough: The page misprints 'part' as 'pant'. Mary Robinson won the Prince of Wales's heart playing the heroine of The Winter's Tale, and was known ever after by the character's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's lost princess in The Winter's Tale became Mary Robinson's lasting nickname after she played the role in 1779.

clue.text: Jeopardize aim, changing the range

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

indicators.note: the letters of the word range change their order

explanation.surface: Altering the range puts the target at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges RANGE into ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something at risk or in peril is to imperil it.

clue.text: Ghost in Hamlet, so-called, no counterfeit

definitions.meaning: Hamlet addresses his father's ghost under the stage with this nickname
a genuine coin, not a fake one, read as a phrase

explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet calls the Ghost by this old word for an honest fellow; split in two it describes a genuine coin rather than a forgery.

clue.text: Archer on horseback grabs one that's discharged

indicators.note: the jockey's first name takes hold of the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: Fred Archer was a famous Victorian jockey
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mounted bowman seizes someone who has been let go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archer on horseback' suggests a mounted bowman; it is Fred Archer, the great nineteenth-century English jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun that is fired is discharged; an employee fired is discharged from a job.

clue.text: Nurse trainee becomes TV opera star

parts.note: an amah is a nursemaid in East and South Asia
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A trainee nurse becomes the star of a televised opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Amahl and the Night Visitors, by Menotti, was the first opera written for television (1951).
explanation.definitionFit: Menotti's opera Amahl and the Night Visitors, made for television, takes its title role from this boy.

clue.text: Laying a basis for the new generation

definitions.text: Laying a basis for the new generation

parts.words: Laying a basis for the new generation
parts.note: reads like founding a movement for young people, but describes releasing an egg ready for fertilisation

explanation.surface: Someone lays the groundwork for a new generation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovulation is the release of an egg from the ovary, the basic step towards conceiving offspring.

clue.text: In a state of restrained apprehension

definitions.text: In a state of restrained apprehension

parts.words: In a state of restrained apprehension
parts.note: reads as nervous but controlled, yet apprehension also means capture, and restrained means held by police

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious but holding it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehension' looks like anxiety; it is an arrest, and 'restrained' is literal custody.
explanation.definitionFit: A person detained by police is held in custody, literally apprehended and restrained.

clue.text: Barman finds fault with junior's veto — a cad's trick

parts.note: a devil is a junior barrister who works for a senior

indicators.note: a trick upon the letters shuffles them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a cad is a scoundrel; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A lawyer objects to a young man's veto as a scoundrel's ploy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is a member of the Bar, a lawyer, not a pub worker. 'trick' rearranges VETO A CAD into ADVOCATE; 'finds fault with' describes what such an advocate does.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil's advocate was the church lawyer arguing against a canonisation, hence a barrister of sorts who argues the contrary.

clue.text: What we pay for excursions

definitions.meaning: trips out, read as goings out

explanation.definitionFit: The word means expenditure, and read literally it means trips away from home.

clue.text: Frank gets over the turbulent Dee in a rush

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits above, over, the other

parts.note: to frank a letter is to mark it with a stamp

indicators.note: the river's name is churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Frank is swept over the choppy River Dee in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it is the verb for marking post. 'turbulent' rearranges DEE into EDE. The Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden mass rush of panicked animals or people.

clue.text: Inflated account rendered by salesman ?

parts.note: a commercial traveller is a salesman, and his story is the proverbial tall tale

explanation.surface: A salesman submits a padded bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account rendered' sounds like an invoice; it is a story told by a commercial traveller, an old British term for a travelling salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is proverbially what a returning voyager tells; a commercial traveller was a salesman.

clue.text: Cut short a game of pontoon ?

parts.note: bridge is a card game, and a pontoon is a floating bridge

explanation.surface: A round of the card game pontoon ends early.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is a British card game, so 'game of pontoon' suggests cards; BRIDGE is both another card game and what a pontoon is.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it while keeping its substance.

clue.text: False report about raising stonecrop to make us supple?

indicators.note: the false statement goes around the upturned plant

parts.note: a lie is a false statement

indicators.note: in a down answer raising turns a word upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: stonecrop, a low creeping sedum, is also called wall moss

explanation.surface: A rumour about growing rock plants that will make us limber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' looks like cultivating; it turns MOSS to SSOM, which LIE wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome means lithe and flexible in body.

clue.text: Etcher's preliminary, impressions of America ?

definitions.meaning: proofs pulled from a plate at stages before it is finished are its ...
the USA is often called the ...

explanation.definitionFit: An etching's successive trial proofs are called its states; and the USA is familiarly the States.

clue.text: La Fontaine perhaps set examination in construction of rheims

indicators.note: the examination is placed inside the rearranged city letters
the city's letters are built into a new arrangement

parts.note: the French city, spelt Reims in French
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A fabulist sets a test in the building of the French cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction of' rearranges the city into M...ISER around ORAL. The English spelling Rheims carries an H the answer lacks; the setter needed Reims.
explanation.definitionFit: La Fontaine wrote fables each ending with a moral, so he is an example of one who draws lessons.

clue.text: Carol composed by Spanish poet

indicators.note: the song's letters are arranged into a new composition

explanation.surface: A Christmas song written by a poet from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges CAROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Garcia Lorca was a celebrated Spanish poet and playwright.

clue.text: Beginning staged for shooting?

definitions.meaning: the start of something, as at the outset
a scene ready for filming is on the set, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Onset means a start; split in two, it says a scene is in place on a film set ready to be shot.

clue.text: Duck down and take cover for the night

definitions.text: Duck down and take cover for the night

parts.words: Duck down and take cover for the night
parts.note: reads as crouching and hiding until dawn, but the sea duck's feathers fill a quilt for the bed

explanation.surface: Someone crouches low and hides until morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a verb; it is the bird, whose down gives the eiderdown, a bed quilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a sea duck whose soft breast feathers stuff the bed quilt named after it.

clue.text: It's a hard job holding the rudder

parts.note: stern means severe or hard
a post is a position or job

explanation.surface: Steering a boat is a tough job.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternpost is the upright timber at a ship's stern on which the rudder is hung.

clue.text: Adopt pose (not in protest)

indicators.note: the protest is taken without the small word that follows it

parts.note: a sit-in is a protest occupying a place
taken as written

explanation.surface: Strike an attitude, but stay out of the demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in' removes IN from SIT-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit for a portrait or photograph is to hold a pose.

clue.text: Turned out with Grace to mend net gale damaged

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, describing someone who is smartly turned out

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A woman named Grace comes out to repair a net ruined by a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' looks like 'arrived'; it means dressed. 'Grace' is a capitalised common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stylishly dressed and graceful is described as refined in appearance.

clue.text: Overheads of retired examiners?

definitions.meaning: a tester is a canopy over a bed, above those who have retired for the night

explanation.definitionFit: A tester is a bed canopy over sleepers who have gone to bed; and those who try things out are examiners.
